newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia to build Formula 1 race track at airport.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia to build Formula 1 race track at airport.

text.p: Malaysia on Friday signed an agreement with a German firm to develop a 250 million ringgit ($99.21 million) Formula One race track which will include hotels, a lake and an orchard.

The 5.6 km-long track, to be built about 4.5 km from the country's new international airport outside the capital city, forms the basis of Malaysia's plan to host a leg of the Formula One championship in 1999.
Malaysia has already agreed to sponsor a team led by triple world motor champion Jackie Stewart for 5.12 million sterling.

At a ceremony on Friday witnessed by Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, Malaysia Airports Bhd, which runs the country's airports, signed a consultancy agreement with Tilke Ingenieure Fur Umwelttechnik for design, construction management and commissioning of the track and facilities.
Construction of the 900-hectare project will start in early 1997 and completion is targeted for third quarter 1998, airport officials said.
"It's not just for Formula One," Mahathir told a news conference to announce the signing. "There are many other races...this is a very comprehensive design."
Airport officials said they expected the facility to also be used for international and domestic sports events such as the Formula 3000.
The 16-metre wide track will have five places for drivers to overtake and the racing circuit facility will include a four-wheel drive track, a motor-cross track and go-kart centre.
A lake will be used for recreational activities such as water sports and will have one luxury and one budget hotel on its shores. A fruit orchard and plant nursery will also be on the grounds.
Another area will have a peat swamp which will be a wetland botanical garden.
Khairuddin Ibrahim, managing director of Malaysia Airports, said the company expected most of the project to be financed with internal funds, adding that it will tap the debt market if necessary.
